_about: The dated setup rows the record's raids in China need (the design director's word of 19:20Z, b375), for the rules builder to lift into setup-1939.json at step 13, beside china-line.json (the raids) and china-stop3.json (ruling 221). Keyed by data file, as the far-side rig lays a seats file. A landing by the book sails only from its own nation's ports (ai.ts landings; the director, 19:12Z, b373), so the Nanning landing of November 1939 (china-line.json 'nanning', ashore at Pakhoi in month 3) sails from Taihoku: the 5th Division is brought there from its 12th Army row in month 2 and lands with the Formosa Army. The historian's word of 19:02Z: under the 21st Army from 16 October 1939 (high); taken from the 12th Army's row (medium); Taihoku stands in for Sanya Bay, Hainan, as the nearest home port. Ruling 224 (the director, 19:19Z, b375, with b387 of 20:07Z; the planner's rows of 20:18Z, forces from the historian, 19:23Z): the 1941 coast raid (china-line.json 'coast41', month 20) sails from Japan's own ports, so its three forces come in month 19, none adding to Japan's lasting strength in China. The 48th Division goes to Formosa, taken from the Formosa Army's row (Formosa is one sea from Foochow, and Taihoku's room is 2). The 13th Army's landing force of about a division goes to Taihoku (one sea from Ningpo and Wenchow), taken from the 13th Army's row at Anking (the planner's choice, by the road down the Yangtze to Shanghai; no source names the division). The Wenchow detachment of about a regiment goes to Taihoku and is lent for its span: struck off in month 22, the month after Wenchow's span of months 20 to 21. All four rows are in the planner's opening-armies.json 'japan_by_date' too (the 25th Army takes the 5th Division in month 27; the 14th Army's row of month 27 takes the 23rd Army's 48th Division, or the Formosa Army's row if that never came): step 13 lays each once.
_1121: The record's rows for China (the design director's rulings of 00:40Z, 00:42Z, 00:43Z, 00:46Z, 03:44Z and 03:47Z of 21 November 2026 on the second rules builder's traces of the six China tests; the historian's china-coast-1941-and-field-armies.md, north-china-oob-and-island-guards.md and china-1944-45-operations.md, accepted as data, the middle of each range). Weights use the game's count, 15,000 men to a division. China's own rows are at China's scale, about 40,000 men to 1.0 for men at a place (the historian's china-scale-restatement.md; the director's 04:51Z). Rows marked 'stops' are the book's own and come only at stops 1 and 2: at stops 3 to 5 the arrivals and departures are the staff's own. The first-day rows ('world' corps) stand at every stop. The 'rows' block amends, by country and name, rows that far-world.json and far-seats-pacific.json lay; each line names its source and leaves when that file's tool takes the figure (far-shores.json, '_src'). The dated choices these rows serve are in china-line.json ('_ops1121').
_coast41: The coast's defenders, as the record placed them (the director's 05:00Z and 05:04Z of 21 November 2026 on the historian's coast-group-armies-and-burma-elites.md; China's scale). After 1937 China held each port with a division or less and kept the main body inland, and the main bodies did not fight for the ports. The seat builder's file laid each group army twice, in its port and inland; here all of a group's rows sum to the record's total, and the places share it in the historian's proportions. The 10th Group Army, 0.55: Ningpo and Chinhai 0.14 and Taichow 0.09, both in Ningpo's province (Haimen was landed on in the same days), Wenchow 0.05, and 0.27 at Chuchow for the Tsientang's south bank and the hills behind Ningpo (Shaohsing and Chuki lie in Hangchow's province, Japan's from the first day, and the hills in Ningpo's; the chart holds a province whole, so the body that stood back is laid one province inland). The 25th Group Army, 0.5: Foochow 0.2, and 0.3 at Nanping for the troops up the Min and those facing Amoy (Tungan, Changchow and Chuanchow lie in Amoy's province, Japan's). Each row is capped at its own weight. Field positions begun and no more at the three ports ('works' 1: the old forts at Chinhai and on the Min were landed round and do not count). The 3rd War Area's reserve on the railway is a later commit's.
_towns: Hangchow and Nanchang each keep a garrison row of 0.4, held and staying (garrison battalions and a mixed brigade's worth: the record's 0.3 to 0.5), so that the 22nd Division at Hangchow and the 11th Army's two divisions at Nanchang are field rows a main effort may take out. No offensive emptied its base town.
_kiangsu: North Kiangsu and the lower Yangtze (the director's 05:08Z, 05:11Z, 05:16Z, 05:18Z and 05:35Z of 21 November 2026 on the historian's haichow-yencheng-and-free-share.md; Japan at 15,000 men to 1.0, China at 40,000). Haichow, taken in March 1939, was held by a detachment of the Hsuchow division with the navy's guard at the port: a town row of 0.175, held and staying, so that the 12th Army's row there is a field row. The sweep of July and August 1941 (the book's stops): Japan's 1.1 as two thin divisions' worth, lent at Nanking for months 23 and 24 (the Grand Canal towns and Taichow lie in Nanking's province). Wang Jingwei's 0.4 is not laid: his regime has no seat. Yencheng's town row of 0.2 comes once the place is Japan's, within the half year. No Chinese row is laid in Yencheng's province. The record's New Fourth Army (its headquarters and 3rd Division, about 0.55, and its 1st Division, 0.5, from January 1941) and Han Deqin's remnant (0.4, to March 1943) lived on the country for years; the province is cut off from China's supply from the first day, a row out of supply starves in its third month, and the game has no row that lives on the country (named for after release). They left Yencheng before Japan came and fought none of the 1941 sweeps, so the sweep walks in, and their weight is carried by China's trait, the war behind the lines. The seat builder's north Kiangsu row stays as it is. The 23rd Army Group (0.75) is what stays at Chuchow when the New Fourth Army's share leaves in month 17: the south Anhwei hills lie in Anking's province on the chart, which Japan holds, and the group's rear base at Tunki lies in Chuchow's. The 33rd Division stands at Nanchang, where the record held it in Kiangsi (Anyi and Fengsin lie in Nanchang's province), by the amendment's 'at'.
_massing: The book's massings, by the planner's own device: a dated row that takes its men from rows on the board ('from'), or is lent for its months ('until'). Second Changsha (September 1941) massed at Yochow, not Nanchang: the 3rd, 4th, 6th and 40th Divisions with four detachments. The 3rd comes from its Sinyang row; the 6th is read as the 11th Army's Yochow row and the 40th as its Kiukiang row (the second rules builder's reading: the planner's rows name no division); the 4th, which no row holds before it sails for Luzon, and the detachments (about a regiment each, 0.8 in all) are lent to month 27. Chekiang (May 1942): the 13th Army gathered about four divisions' worth at Hangchow. The 22nd is there; the 15th comes whole from Nanking and goes home in month 37 under its own name, so the planner's row of month 54 still finds it; the parts of the 32nd and 116th (1.0) and the mixed brigades (0.9) are lent to month 37. Nanchang's two divisions are the Kiangsi thrust's and need no row.
_north: North China's order of battle, about 21 pieces: the independent mixed brigades as their own rows of 0.375, held and staying, at the historian's places (marked L). New rows: the 2nd at Kalgan; the 3rd at Lishih and the 9th at Taiyuan; the 1st at Tangshan, the 8th at Shihkiachwang and the 15th at Tientsin; the 6th at Chefoo, the 7th at Lintsing and the 10th at Tsinan. Three of the planner's rows are re-weighed to one brigade each: the 1st Army's brigades at Taiyuan (the 4th), its western Shansi row (the 16th) and Tsingtao's garrison (the 5th). The planner's 27th stands at Peiping and its 110th at Anyang, so Tientsin takes the 15th Brigade and Paoting has nobody; Sintai, and Mengkiang beyond Kalgan, had no brigade of their own. At the book's stops the four brigades raised to divisions follow the record's months: the 59th (month 30, from the 10th, Tsinan), the 69th (30, from the 16th, Lishih), the 62nd (46, from the 4th and 6th, Taiyuan; the planner's row of month 55 takes it to Kaifeng) and the 63rd (46, from the 15th, at Peiping as the 27th leaves for Manchuria). The departures the planner's rows already carry keep their months. Two wait on rows in the south that no file has: the 41st for Wewak (months 41 to 42) and the 36th for Sarmi (month 52). The collaborator troops are named in the historian's file and not laid.
_hunan: The Hunan push of May 1944 (the book's stops): the 11th Army's seven divisions on a broad front, about 8 to 9 forward with its army troops, never four rows. A western group (the 40th and 116th) and a centre (the 34th, 58th and 68th) at Yochow, an eastern group (the 3rd and 13th) at Nanchang, each a corps row formed from the 11th Army's rows on the board; the 39th stays at Ichang, held. The 58th and 68th were raised in 1942 from brigades no row of the game holds, and the 39th joined in 1940, so the centre's third division and the 39th are new to the board (2.0). The planner's rows bring the 64th, the 27th, the 37th and the army troops. Changsha keeps a garrison of 0.4 once it is Japan's (the record's 0.3 to 0.5), so no field row is pinned there. It and the 39th are formed where they stand (their 'from' names no row of the board), so neither is brought ashore anywhere else: each waits its half year for its place and is then struck. (No row of Japan's is a levy.)
_1945: The 1944 coast landings sail from Japan's own ports as the 1941 raids did: Wenchow's force (0.55) from Taihoku, Foochow's (0.5, with naval landing troops) from Formosa. Kukong and Kanchow (January and February 1945): the 23rd Army's brigades (1.0) join the rows at Canton; the northern end is the Hunan push's own rows. Laohokow and Siangyang (March 1945): the 110th and 115th Divisions, the 3rd Tank Division and the 4th Cavalry Brigade are formed up at Sinyang from the 12th Army's rows in month 66, and the 39th is freed at Ichang.
_canton: Canton's rows as the record had them (the design director's rulings of 07:52Z, 07:55Z, 08:10Z and 08:48Z of 22 November 2026 on the second rules builder's Nanning trace; the historian's canton-rows-1939-45.md, laid as facts, the middle of each range). The chart's '21st Army (Canton)' is the 104th Division, the one formation at Canton from the first month to the last: it keeps its name (a row is not re-formed for a label) and stands at 1.0, the chart's full division, as the 18th Division does at Tungkun, which is counted with Canton. A square division's fourth regiment is a row of its own: the 104th's 170th Infantry, 0.3 at Canton from the first month, which left in January 1941 to become the 21st Independent Mixed Brigade in Indochina. On the chart Indochina's force comes with Japan's demand, so at every stop the regiment stands at Canton until the demand's month, and Hanoi's post is then made from it wherever it stands (pacific.json, 'posts', the fourth word; the design director's ruling of 08:48Z): its men are counted once. Where no demand comes it stands and is its staff's. The 38th Division (from 2) ends at the book's stops in 30, as its regiments' rows sail for the Indies (the Ito Detachment in 29, the Shoji Detachment and the 229th Infantry in 30): it was counted twice from 1942. At stops 3 to 5 it comes as its three regiments and nothing ends. The 51st Division, 1.0, at Canton from September 1941 (25), one row at every stop: at the book's stops the book stands it at Rabaul from November 1942 (39), a station of the book's own later months (china-line.json, '_station51'; the design director's 08:10Z, 5, and 08:48Z, 2), so its end at 39 is a move and nobody is struck off; at stops 3 to 5 it stands as its staff's, for it was not lent for a place. The 19th and 22nd Independent Mixed Brigades, 0.35 each, raised at Canton in 1941-42: January 1942 (29), the middle of the range. The 129th and 130th Divisions, about 0.6 each, formed in April 1945 (68); the 130th is raised from the 19th brigade, one row becoming the other. Quality by this file's own scale: a brigade 0.2, a division raised from a brigade 0.1 (the 63rd's), the 51st the 38th's 0.3, the 170th its division's 0.35. The 23rd Independent Mixed Brigade, which led on the road to Nanning in 1944, has no row: none is laid without the historian's size and month.
